 Appearance:
Shri R.N. Dave, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Akshansh Mehra, advocate appearing through vid  on behalf of Shri Sanjay Mehra, learned counsel for the respo  ORDER

Learned counsel for the appellant, at the outset, submits that he does not wish to press I.A.
No.1283/2024.
Accordingly, I.A. No.1283/2024 is dismissed as not pressed.
2. The present appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 26.11.2010 passed in Claim Case No.33/2009 challenging the quantum of compensation.
3. All the respondents are duly served, however, respondent Nos.1 and 2 did not chose to appear before this Court, hence, the matter is being heard in their absence.
4. The claims tribunal has directed the insurance company to first pay and then recover from the owner and driver.

5. The short facts of the case are that on 17.11.2008 at around 10.30 a.m., 2 MA-624-2011 the appellant was going by his motorcycle from Sanwer to Umariya village, when he reached near Pushpgiri road, the respondent No.1 came driving Pick-up vehicle bearing registration number MP41-GA-0152 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of the appellant because of which he sustained grievous injuries on different parts of his body.
He suffered multiple fractures in femur bone of his right leg.
6. The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the aforesaid accident.
The claims tribunal after recording the evidence quantified the amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.2,06,000/-.

1 7.

The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the amount of compensation is not adequate for the reason that the permanent disability has been taken by the tribunal at 15% with the respect to loss of earning capacity, however, as per the statement of Dr. Y.C. Pandey, AW-3 the appellant suffered 53.3% permanent disability into his right lower limb.

He thus points out that looking to the fact that the appellant was working as a labourer as he was running the shop of puncture repair of tyres, thus, the said permanent disability in right leg has substantially affected the capacity of the appellant to continue his business.
He further points out that the appellant remained under treatment for long period.
The implant of rod was also inserted into his right leg.

As such,
considering the above facts the amount of compensation is meager.
He, thus, prays for enhancement of compensation by considering the permanent disability as 25%.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for insurance company straight way refers 3 MA-624-2011 to para 9 of the impugned award as well as the cross-examination of AW-3 Dr. Y.C. Pandey.
He submits that in his cross examination the doctor has accepted that to the extent of half inch shortening, the same is not considered as any permanent disability.
He also points out that the said doctor has also admitted in his cross examination that the bones have properly been united and there is no malunion.
He thus submits that in fact the extent of 15% has been taken by the claims tribunal rather on higher side, hence, no interference is warranted in the impugned award.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10.

Considering the fact that there is proper union of bones after the implant was inserted and also fact that the witness of claimants himself has stated that upto half inch shortening same is not considered as permanent disability in medical terms.
This Court is not inclined to enhance the permanent disability with respect to loss of earning capacity.
As such, no interference is warranted in the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 9 of the award.
However, from perusal of Ex.P-11 to Ex.P-17 and the documents relating to treatment Ex.P-19 to Ex.P-361, it is seen that the appellant has suffered multiple fractures in his right lower limb.
He was operated upon repeatedly and internal/external fixators were applied.
The treatment continued upto one year.
As such, in the considered view of this Court, the appellant deserves for an additional amount of Rs.75000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
As such, it is hereby directed that further amount of Rs.75000/- be paid to the appellant.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of 4 MA-624-2011 the application before the claims tribunal.
11. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
Pappu vs Rajesh And 02 Ors.
